newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SHORT, RATES MIXED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SHORT, RATES MIXED.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market continued short on Thursday on a lack of major maturing treasury bills with dealers saying short-term trading rates were mixed to firmer.
"There are no major maturities up to 29th October. If there were the Reserve Bank was going to pump in money through the sale of treasury bills," one dealer said.
The dealers said discount houses went to tender at a rate of 19.60 at Thursday's auction from 19.73 percent last week so that they could sell large volumes of treasury bills which they were holding.
But the rates for NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days remained high at 24 percent (buying) and 22.5 percent (selling) compared to Wednesday's 23.5 and 22.5 percent.
Bankers' acceptances were being bought at 23.5 percent versus 21 percent and sold unchanged at 20.5 percent.
The call rate added another percentage point to 23 percent in a market short of Z$128.4 million.
